retained_skill: Recognize and fix SSRF by validating both the initial URL and every redirect destination against the blocked-host and blocked-network policy while preserving successful external fetches.
bottleneck: The image promises an existing pytest suite but ships neither /tests/test_outputs.py nor pytest. All 12 scored attempts therefore invented replacement tests, passed those, and submitted implementations that the unavailable grader exercised differently; ten then failed five redirect/allowed-fetch checks, and two renamed the existing policy class and failed seven imports.
change: Repair the broken setup by installing pytest and shipping the existing test suite in the image, while repairing its transport mock so it accepts both the seed's module-level urlopen and an equivalent custom urllib opener. This structural repair removes test reconstruction outside the retained skill and lets the original test failures directly signal whether initial and redirected destinations are validated.
restore: A later version can remove the shipped suite and bundled pytest after the student reliably preserves the existing interface and validates redirects from the public policy alone; the SSRF validation requirement itself is unchanged.
prediction: When the suite is present, attempts will run it instead of writing a guessed replacement, see redirect or allowed-fetch failures against their actual implementation, and revise the fetch path rather than submitting after a self-authored green suite. This is refuted if attempts still replace /tests/test_outputs.py before using it, or if they use the shipped failures but still submit with redirect/allowed-fetch failures. I predict 5 of 12 will solve: attempt 09's near-complete implementation and several of the ten 5/10 implementations should now receive actionable feedback, while class-renaming and overengineered rewrites should continue to fail.
